newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen consolidating.

text.p: Australian bond and foreign exchange markets are expected to consolidate early in the week ahead after last week's local rate cut and the yen's surge against the U.S. and Australian dollars.

Direction is expected from the United States early in the week, given a lack of domestic data, but the focus briefly returns home on Thursday when the final Australian average weekly earnings data for the quarter to August is released.

"With virtually all of the good news now priced in, further gains will be limited and will likely require further support from the U.S. bond market," ANZ said of the local bond market in its weekly update.
Housing finance data on Monday is seen unlikely to move the market, but there is some interest in the finalised wages data on Thursday.

"The surprisingly good outcome implied by the preliminary release of this series was essentially the reason the RBA was able to ease again," Commonwealth Bank said in its weekly outlook, adding that the market should watch for possible upward revisions.
Equity markets are seen focusing overall on Wall Street's teeterings as it lurches to and from new highs.
Results from Westpac Banking Corp, St George Bank Ltd CSR Ltd and News Corp and a rash of annual meetings should provide the individual highlights.

For Monday, the Dow's 14 point rise to yet another record high should set the tone, but local sentiment remains hesitant as managing directors continue to issue disappointing first quarter comments at the current round of annual meetings.
On bond markets, a quiet morning is expected given the near steady performance of 10 year bond futures on SYCOM.
The Australian dollar however is set to open back in more familiar territory at US$0.7875 thanks to New York buyers on Friday night, having closed locally down at US$0.7835 on Friday.
"A continued re-rating of Australia from offshore and associated strong investor demand are providing good support," ANZ said.
BONDS (Fri: 10 yr cash yield 7.21 percent, 3 yr 6.58 pct)
Australian bonds will be looking to consolidate this week after the wild swings of the past few days and in the absence of any major economic data.
Ten year bond futures rose half a basis point to 92.785 on SYCOM, ensuring a quiet Monday morning's trade as long as their are no major surprises with the housing data.

Last week's 50 basis point cut in official interest rates to 6.50 percent had been expected, and already analysts are contemplating the possibility of a further easing in this cycle with the economy still deemed to be in need of a push.
A Reuters survey of economists on Friday gave a 50 percent probability of a further 50 basis points being lopped off rates, and probabaly in the first quarter of next year.
Meanwhile, 10-year bond yields will be looking to bed down around the 7.25 percent area before pressing on towards 7.0 percent, analysts said.
The market should start the week steady to a touch weaker after U.S. Treasuries edged back on Friday after sharp gains on Thursday.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: US$0.7835, New York US$0.7875)
The Australian dollar will open firmer on Monday thanks to U.S. support on Friday but doubts remain about its longer term future.

The Australian dollar will be vulnerable on the downside after tumbling though three month old support at US$0.7855 last week as the market began to reassess the risk of Japanese interest rates rising.
"Some cracks have just started to appear in the Australian dollar," Commonwealth Bank analysts said in a commentary.

"The current fundamental position of the Australian dollar is somewhat weaker than the U.S. dollar. Commodity prices continue to put in a lacklustre performance while further domestic easing speculation is likely to persist over the next couple of months," the analysts said.
The concerns were considered premature by most analysts but still served to drive Japanese bond yields sharply higher and so narrowed the yield advantage enjoyed by A$ and US$ assets.
The Japanese authorities also signalled an end to their policy of driving down the yen's value, which saw both the local and U.S. dollar lose over two yen in as many days.

The Australian unit had found good support at US$0.7810/20 from domestic exporters and Asian banks, but dealers feared this could be overwhelmed if last week's profit taking turned into a more generalised re-rating against high yielding currencies.

In such a case the dollar could sink to US$0.7750 next week, on its way towards August's low around 77 cents. A rally back above US$0.7890 was needed to forestall that risk and it would take a break of US$0.7945 to revive the currency's old uptrend.
The domestic data due this week were of only secondary importance and, anyway, the market's reaction would be coloured by its preoccupation with monetary policy.
Thus a big rise in housing finance would be mildly dollar supportive since it would suggest the housing market was recovering without the need of another cut in rates.
AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries 2,362.1, up 15.4)

While the market looked firmer on Friday, concerns remained about the local market's ability to cope with a U.S. market that may come off its record highs as election euphoria fades. Friday's positive finish to the week put a spring back in some trader's steps although confidence could not be said to be high.
"I don't know how well we will react to a negative day over there," said a Sydney broker.
Economic data due next week is of a relatively minor nature with consumer sentiment on Wednesday probably the pick.
The annual meeting season continues apace with a number of major ones due as are some profit results.
Profit results are due from CSR on Monday and from Westpac and News Corp on Tuesday.
Burns Philp and Co Ltd holds its annual meeting on Monday, while Westfield Holdings and Mayne Nickless hold their annual meetings on Tuesday.

On Wednesday FAI Insurance holds its annual meeting. Arnotts, MIM Holdings and Woolworths have their meetings on Thursday while Goodman Fielder, Pacific dunlop and WMC Ltd are expected to have their meetings on Friday.
